title: Quitting your job
titleChinese: 辞还是不辞？跳槽对个人发展的利与弊
paragraphs: How long have you been in your job for? If you’re climbing a career ladder, how long do you intend to stay on it? It’s hard to know when to jump ship and to do something different, and it’s even more problematic deciding whether to quit if you don’t have a new job to go to.

In the past, a job for life was just that – something you did throughout your working life. Being loyal to one company came with many perks and job security. But these days, there are many more opportunities to switch your career path, so it’s normal to have many jobs listed on your CV. It’s accepted that our goals change, so quitting one job for another shows how versatile and adaptable we are.

According to insurance firm LV, a worker in the UK will change employer every five years on average. In the US, it’s even shorter, with people staying with a single employer for just over four years, according to official statistics. Victoria Bethlehem from recruitment firm Adecco told the BBC that she looks favourably on a prospective employee who has changed roles every three to five years.

While it’s good to pursue new work challenges, is quitting your job for no job at all career suicide? It’s risky, but it can give you a chance to follow your dreams. LinkedIn influencer Murugan Pandian, who’s a project efficiency expert at St Joseph’s Hospital Health Center, says: “If you are that miserable [in your job], then sometimes it helps to quit, reassess your priorities in life and then come up with a more creative job-hunting strategy.”

Of course resigning from your job is scary – there is the fear of the unknown, but for some, no job is better than a thankless one. The recent Covid pandemic has certainly made people think twice about their career priorities, and with workers being forced back to the office, some of them may be tempted to leave their job without having a new role to go to. But no job means no money, so quitting needs careful thought, although it could lead you down a whole new career path.

vocabulary.entry: career ladder /kəˈrɪə ˈlædə/ 职业阶梯
vocabulary.example: She is determined to climb the career ladder in the marketing industry.
vocabulary.translation: 她决心在营销行业攀登职业阶梯。

vocabulary.entry: jump ship /dʒʌmp ʃɪp/ 跳槽；离职
vocabulary.example: He decided to jump ship when he got a better offer from a rival firm.
vocabulary.translation: 收到竞争对手公司的更好邀约时，他决定跳槽。

vocabulary.entry: quit /kwɪt/ v. 辞职；放弃
vocabulary.example: She plans to quit her job and travel around the world for a year.
vocabulary.translation: 她打算辞职，花一年时间环游世界。

vocabulary.entry: job for life /dʒɒb fɔː laɪf/ 终身职业
vocabulary.example: A job for life is rare in today's fast-changing job market.
vocabulary.translation: 在如今瞬息万变的就业市场，终身职业已经很少见了。

vocabulary.entry: loyal /ˈlɔɪəl/ adj. 忠诚的
vocabulary.example: He has remained loyal to the company for more than twenty years.
vocabulary.translation: 他已经忠诚于这家公司二十多年了。

vocabulary.entry: perk /pɜːk/ n. 额外福利
vocabulary.example: Free gym membership is one of the perk of working here.
vocabulary.translation: 免费健身房会员资格是在这里工作的一项额外福利。

vocabulary.entry: job security /dʒɒb sɪˈkjʊərəti/ 工作稳定性
vocabulary.example: Government jobs usually offer high job security.
vocabulary.translation: 政府部门的工作通常具有很高的工作稳定性。

vocabulary.entry: career path /kəˈrɪə pɑːθ/ 职业道路
vocabulary.example: She is still exploring different career paths to find her passion.
vocabulary.translation: 她还在探索不同的职业道路，寻找自己真正热爱的方向。

vocabulary.entry: CV /ˌsiː ˈviː/ n. 简历
vocabulary.example: You should update your CV before applying for new positions.
vocabulary.translation: 申请新岗位前，你应该更新自己的简历。

vocabulary.entry: versatile /ˈvɜːsətaɪl/ adj. 多才多艺的；多面手的
vocabulary.example: The versatile designer can work on both fashion and interior projects.
vocabulary.translation: 这位多才多艺的设计师既能做时尚设计，也能做室内设计项目。

vocabulary.entry: adaptable /əˈdæptəbl/ adj. 能适应的
vocabulary.example: Successful entrepreneurs are highly adaptable to market changes.
vocabulary.translation: 成功的企业家能高度适应市场变化。

vocabulary.entry: employer /ɪmˈplɔɪə/ n. 雇主
vocabulary.example: Her employer praised her for her excellent performance last quarter.
vocabulary.translation: 她的雇主称赞她上季度的出色表现。

vocabulary.entry: official statistic /əˈfɪʃl stəˈtɪstɪk/ 官方统计数据
vocabulary.example: The official statistic indicates a steady growth in the tech sector.
vocabulary.translation: 官方统计数据显示科技行业正在稳步增长。

vocabulary.entry: recruitment firm /rɪˈkruːtmənt fɜːm/ 招聘公司
vocabulary.example: The recruitment firm specialises in matching candidates with senior roles.
vocabulary.translation: 这家招聘公司专门为高级岗位匹配候选人。

vocabulary.entry: prospective employee /prəˈspektɪv ɪmˈplɔɪiː/ 潜在员工
vocabulary.example: The interview is designed to evaluate the prospective employee’s competence.
vocabulary.translation: 这场面试旨在评估潜在员工的能力。

vocabulary.entry: pursue /pəˈsjuː/ v. 追求；致力于
vocabulary.example: He left his stable job to pursue a career in music.
vocabulary.translation: 他辞掉了稳定的工作，追求音乐事业。

vocabulary.entry: career suicide /kəˈrɪə ˈsuːɪsaɪd/ 职业自杀
vocabulary.example: Speaking ill of your former boss in an interview is career suicide.
vocabulary.translation: 面试时说前老板的坏话无异于职业自杀。

vocabulary.entry: influencer /ˈɪnfluənsə/ n. 网红；有影响力的人
vocabulary.example: The social media influencer has collaborated with several famous brands.
vocabulary.translation: 这位社交媒体网红已经和多个知名品牌合作过。

vocabulary.entry: reassess /ˌriːəˈses/ v. 重新评估
vocabulary.example: After the failure, she had to reassess her approach to the project.
vocabulary.translation: 经历失败后，她不得不重新评估自己的项目方案。

vocabulary.entry: priority /praɪˈɒrəti/ n. 优先事项；优先级
vocabulary.example: Work-life balance is her top priority when choosing a job.
vocabulary.translation: 选择工作时，工作与生活的平衡是她的首要优先事项。

vocabulary.entry: job-hunting strategy /ˈdʒɒb hʌntɪŋ ˈstrætədʒi/ 求职策略
vocabulary.example: The expert shared some effective job-hunting strategy for fresh graduates.
vocabulary.translation: 这位专家为应届毕业生分享了一些有效的求职策略。

vocabulary.entry: resign /rɪˈzaɪn/ v. 辞职
vocabulary.example: He resigned from his position as manager due to health issues.
vocabulary.translation: 由于健康问题，他辞去了经理一职。

vocabulary.entry: thankless /ˈθæŋkləs/ adj. 费力不讨好的
vocabulary.example: Being a volunteer is a thankless job but it brings great satisfaction.
vocabulary.translation: 做志愿者是一份费力不讨好的工作，但能带来极大的满足感。

vocabulary.entry: think twice /θɪŋk twaɪs/ 三思；慎重考虑
vocabulary.example: You should think twice before making a decision to quit without a backup plan.
vocabulary.translation: 没有备用计划就决定辞职，你应该三思而后行。

vocabulary.entry: tempt /tempt/ v. 引诱；诱惑
vocabulary.example: The chance to work abroad tempted her to apply for the transfer.
vocabulary.translation: 出国工作的机会诱惑她申请了调任。

sentences.english: How long have you been in your job for?
sentences.chinese: 你已经在现在的岗位上工作多久了？

sentences.english: If you’re climbing a career ladder, how long do you intend to stay on it?
sentences.chinese: 如果你正在攀登职业阶梯，打算在这条路上走多久？

sentences.english: It’s hard to know when to jump ship and to do something different, and it’s even more problematic deciding whether to quit if you don’t have a new job to go to.
sentences.chinese: 很难判断何时该跳槽去尝试新的领域，而如果还没找到下家就决定辞职，那更是难上加难。

sentences.english: In the past, a job for life was just that – something you did throughout your working life.
sentences.chinese: 过去，“终身职业”名副其实——就是你整个职业生涯都在从事的工作。

sentences.english: Being loyal to one company came with many perks and job security.
sentences.chinese: 对一家公司保持忠诚会带来诸多福利和工作稳定性。

sentences.english: But these days, there are many more opportunities to switch your career path, so it’s normal to have many jobs listed on your CV.
sentences.chinese: 但如今，更换职业道路的机会变得更多，所以简历上罗列多份工作经历是很正常的事。

sentences.english: It’s accepted that our goals change, so quitting one job for another shows how versatile and adaptable we are.
sentences.chinese: 人们的目标会不断变化，这一点已被普遍接受，因此为了另一份工作而辞职，恰恰能体现一个人的多才多艺和适应能力。

sentences.english: According to insurance firm LV, a worker in the UK will change employer every five years on average.
sentences.chinese: 据英国LV保险公司的数据显示，英国职场人士平均每五年就会更换一次雇主。

sentences.english: In the US, it’s even shorter, with people staying with a single employer for just over four years, according to official statistics.
sentences.chinese: 官方统计数据表明，在美国，这个周期更短，人们在同一位雇主手下的工作时长仅略超四年。

sentences.english: Victoria Bethlehem from recruitment firm Adecco told the BBC that she looks favourably on a prospective employee who has changed roles every three to five years.
sentences.chinese: 德科招聘公司的维多利亚·伯利恒在接受BBC采访时表示，她对那些每三到五年就更换一次岗位的潜在雇员抱有好感。

sentences.english: While it’s good to pursue new work challenges, is quitting your job for no job at all career suicide?
sentences.chinese: 虽然追求新的工作挑战是件好事，但没找到下家就辞职，算得上是职业自杀吗？

sentences.english: It’s risky, but it can give you a chance to follow your dreams.
sentences.chinese: 这种做法确实有风险，但它能给你一个追逐梦想的机会。

sentences.english: LinkedIn influencer Murugan Pandian, who’s a project efficiency expert at St Joseph’s Hospital Health Center, says: “If you are that miserable [in your job], then sometimes it helps to quit, reassess your priorities in life and then come up with a more creative job-hunting strategy.”
sentences.chinese: 领英网红、圣约瑟夫医院健康中心的项目效率专家穆鲁甘·潘迪安表示：“如果你在当前工作中已经痛苦到这种地步，那么有时候辞职是有用的——你可以重新评估自己的人生优先级，然后制定出更有创意的求职策略。”

sentences.english: Of course resigning from your job is scary – there is the fear of the unknown, but for some, no job is better than a thankless one.
sentences.chinese: 当然，辞职这件事本身是令人恐慌的——人们总会对未知的事物感到恐惧，但对有些人来说，失业也比做一份费力不讨好的工作要强。

sentences.english: The recent Covid pandemic has certainly made people think twice about their career priorities, and with workers being forced back to the office, some of them may be tempted to leave their job without having a new role to go to.
sentences.chinese: 近年来的新冠疫情无疑让人们重新审视自己的职业优先级，而随着企业强制员工重返办公室，有些人可能会忍不住在没找到新工作的情况下就离职。

sentences.english: But no job means no money, so quitting needs careful thought, although it could lead you down a whole new career path.
sentences.chinese: 但失业意味着没有收入，所以辞职需要深思熟虑，不过，这也可能引领你踏上一条全新的职业道路。
